$comment: Victron Venus plugin configuration. The Cerbo GX is reached over plain MQTT on the boat network; the simulator's emulated Cerbo answers on the same protocol, so this file is identical on the boat and on the bench apart from the host. Instance mappings give a device a stable Signal K name, otherwise its paths carry the raw Victron instance number, which can change if the device is reset or swapped. The battery mapping below is not a guess: read directly off Cinderella's real Cerbo on 2026-08-14 by subscribing to its MQTT topic tree (com.victronenergy.battery, instance 279, a BMV-712 Smart on VE.Direct). There is currently no solar charger or inverter/charger connected to this Cerbo at all — confirmed the same way, not merely quiet — so no mapping is given for either; the simulator still emits synthetic data for both (for testing the marina/anchored dashboards), which will appear under its own raw instance numbers rather than a named path until real hardware exists to map. Add an entry here the same way the battery one was found: subscribe to N/+/+/#, publish an empty message to R/<portalId>/system/0/Serial to prompt a state dump, and read the instance number back from the topic path.
